messages.author: eaf891916146cc5e
messages.subject: Replicating Friedman & Miyake (2004; JEP:GEN)
parts:
Hi lavaan users,


I´m trying to replicate the second model of Friedman & Miyake (2004; JEP:GEN, pp. 114, part A) with lavaan. Here is the model:


 


So far, my syntax looks like that:

m <- '

  # latent variables

    inhibition of pre-potent response =~ antisaccade + stroop + stop-signal

    resistance to distracter interference =~ flanker + word-naming + shape-matching

    list 1 recall =~ Brown-Peterson list1 + AB-AC-AD AB trials + cued recall 1-block

    list 2 recall =~ Brown-Peterson list2 + AB-AC-AD AB trials + cued recall 2-block

  # regressions

    list 2 recall ~ list 1 recall

  # error variances

    list 2 recall ~~ inhibition of pre-potent response

    list 2 recall ~~ resistance to distracter interference

    Brown-Peterson list1 ~~ Brown-Peterson list2

    AB-AC-AD AB trials ~~ AB-AC-AD AC trials

    cued recall 1-block ~~ cued recall 2-block '


This gives me the following model:


 

In comparison with Friedman & Miyake´s (2004) model, in my model, the residual variance of list 2 recall is not considered as the latent variable “resistance to proactive interference” (the difference between both models are presented in red in the first figure).  

Therefore, my question: How do I have to write the syntax to get the first figure?


Thanks in advance for any response!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Replicating Friedman & Miyake (2004; JEP:GEN)
parts: Therefore, my question: How do I have to write the syntax to get the first figure?

Define the factor as a second-order construct with a single indicator (list 2) by fixing the residual variance of list 2 to zero and the "loading" to 1, so that all the residual variance is represented by "resistance to proactive interference"

resistance to proactive interference =~ 1*list2recall
list2recall ~~ 0*list2recall
resistance to proactive interference ~~ NA*resistance to proactive interference

FYI, you can't actually have spaces in the variable names.  If they have spaces in your data frame, rename them replacing spaces with periods or underscores.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

parts:
Hi!

Following your last message, I computed the model with the restrictions included in the model presented in the first figure, i.e.,

m2 <- '
  # latent variables
    pr =~ antisaccade + stroopeffect + stopsignal
    di =~ flankereffect + wordnaming_int + shapematching_int
    l1r =~ brownpeterson_list1 + abacad_ab + cuedrecall_block1
    l2r =~ brownpeterson_list2 + abacad_ac + cuedrecall_block2
pi =~ -1*l2r

# regressions 
    l2r ~ l1r
# (co)variances

brownpeterson_list1 ~~ brownpeterson_list2
    abacad_ab ~~ abacad_ac
    cuedrecall_block1 ~~ cuedrecall_block2

pr ~~ 0*l2r
    di ~~ 0*l2r
    pi ~~ 0*l1r
    l2r ~~ 0*l2r
    pi ~~ NA*pi '
fit <- sem(m2, sample.cov = tmp_cov, sample.nobs = sample_size, std.lv = TRUE, estimator = "ML")
But I got the same error message as before, that is:

Warning message:
In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
  lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

Then, I removed the last line of the syntax (i.e.,  pi ~~ NA*pi) and thus computed the model. In this case, it worked and I got all relevant values, except the variance of the latent variable pi which was 1. In the original model published by Friedman & Miyake (2004), however, this residual variance was computed and was found to be 0.32. I most probably got the error message in my first computation, because in the syntax I asked to estimate freely the variance of pi (with pi ~~ NA*pi), but in the sem function, I set it to 1 (with std.lv = TRUE). Thus, is there a way to estimate freely the variance of one latent variable and to fix the residual variance of the other latent variables to 1?

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Replicating Friedman & Miyake (2004; JEP:GEN)
parts: is there a way to estimate freely the variance of one latent variable and to fix the residual variance of the other latent variables to 1?
Yes, that is why I put the "NA" for the variance parameter.  Model syntax will override any defaults you set in your sem() call.
